reader.requirement: At --std 85 a WRITE to an indexed file in random or (level 2) dynamic access mode, open OUTPUT or I-O, must accept records in any order of prime key values: no ascending-sequence check (the GR14 '21' belongs only to sequential access), each record stored and retrievable in key order, and the file position indicator untouched (GR5).

edition-consulted.switches: InForce (Year < 2002): the 85 mandatory INVALID KEY / USE (SR3), not the release order

reader.edition-search: IndexedConnector.Write selects the ordering rule from the ACCESS MODE alone (sequentialRelease = Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential; _lastWrittenPrime compared only then); no Edition / DialectBehaviors test on the path (grep of DialectBehaviors.IsActive in Runtime/IO: no WRITE site in IndexedConnector). The OPEN EXTEND refusal for non-sequential access is the binder's, edition-blind.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness l1c38 writes out of key order in one access mode; not exercised there: dynamic access in OUTPUT and I-O, interleaving with START/READ NEXT (FPI unaffected), the sequential-access contrast, and EXTEND on a non-sequential file.

probes.printed: random OUTPUT R90,R10,R50,R05: WR 00 each, random READ R05 -> 00; dynamic OUTPUT D9X,D5Y,D1X: 00/02/02 (02 = duplicate alternate); dynamic I-O after START = D5Y: WD 02 D0Z, WD 02 D7X, then READ NEXT N1 00 D5Y, N2 00 D7X; sequential READ back D0Z D1X D5Y D7X D9X
probes.expected: §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR15 any program-specified order; GR5 FPI unaffected by WRITE

probes.printed: sequential access OUTPUT S50 then S10: S1 00, USE-S 21, S2 21
probes.expected: GR14/GR17a: the any-order licence does not extend to sequential access

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL2372 OPEN EXTEND 'IXD' — the file's access mode is DYNAMIC; EXTEND requires sequential access
probes.expected: §1985:IX.4.4.3 SR1: EXTEND only in sequential access mode, so GR15's modes are OUTPUT and I-O only

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR15  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR15 ["records may be released to the mass storage control system (MSCS) in any program-specified order"]
OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14  the text is in GR14 ["records must be released to the mass storage control system (MSCS) in ascending order of prime record key values"]
OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR5  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5
OK  §1985:IX.4.4.3 SR1  (4.4.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The ordering test in IndexedConnector.Write is keyed on the access mode alone, so random and dynamic WRITEs never raise '21'; descending, interleaved and mid-positioning writes all succeeded and read back in key order, and a WRITE between START and READ NEXT left the position intact.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-010/wu.cob at --std 85: RANDOM access in I-O mode (the reader probed random only in OUTPUT): WRITE K090, K010, K005 in descending order after earlier K050 -> 'W6 00', 'W7 00', 'W8 00', random READ K005 -> K005B3fiv; no '21' sequence check. Reader's sequential contrast (21) and EXTEND-on-dynamic refusal (COBOL2372) stand. cite.py: 'OK §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR15 (4.9.4 General Rules) the text is in GR15' [in any program-specified order].
